question: Who among the following was granted the title of ‘Chief of the Merchants’ or Malikut-Tujjar by the Bahamani ruler, Humayun Shah?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahmud Gawan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahmud Gawan was a notable figure in the Bahamani Sultanate and served as a prime minister under several rulers.
 
• He was a Persian merchant and a statesman who rose to prominence in the Bahamani court due to his administrative and diplomatic skills.
 
• Humayun Shah, the Bahamani ruler, granted him the title of 'Chief of the Merchants' or Malikut-Tujjar in recognition of his contributions to the state and his influence in trade and commerce.
 
• Mahmud Gawan played a crucial role in the expansion and consolidation of the Bahamani Sultanate during his tenure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mahmud Gawan was known for his reforms in the administrative, military, and economic sectors of the Bahamani Sultanate.
 
• He established a network of markets and trade routes which enhanced the economic stability of the region.
 
• His contributions also extended to the cultural and educational fields, where he founded the famous madrasa in Bidar, which became a center of learning and culture.
 
• Despite his achievements, Mahmud Gawan faced political intrigue and was eventually executed in 1481 due to a conspiracy against him.
